paragraphs.section: Miscellaneous

paragraphs.text: This set's suite of supported color pairs has not been seen before in Magic . While supporting a mix of ally and enemy color pairs has been previously done in the three blocks on Ravnica and Lorwyn Eclipsed , they overlapped twice in combinations. The combination seen here can be described as "enemy colors, with red and white inverted".
paragraphs.section: Miscellaneous

paragraphs.text: The set does not have any artifact creature cards; their only presence in the set is the token created by Stone-Giant of High Pass . It is the first such premier set since Guildpact was printed more than 20 years prior.
paragraphs.section: Miscellaneous

paragraphs.text: The 2/2 Dwarf creature token has the printed type line "Tolkien Creature — Dwarf" as a tribute to the book's author, J. R. R. Tolkien . This type line honor was previously used on the 1/1 Halfling token in The Lord of the Rings: Tales of Middle-earth Commander .
paragraphs.section: Cards

paragraphs.text: Thanks to the brevity of The Hobbit , several cards in the set reference characters and concepts that do not, properly speaking, appear in the book: The Queen of Dale is supposed to be Bard the Bowman's wife after he becomes King of Dale. She isn't mentioned anywhere in the book, although a son is mentioned in The Lord of the Rings . Desert Were-Worm is only attested in a figurative expression spoken by Bilbo at one point. Neither the worms nor the desert they live in appear in person.
paragraphs.section: Cards

paragraphs.text: The vertical cycle of Bears abandons the longstanding tradition that an ordinary bear is a 2/2 creature that costs two mana . When asked about the subject, Mark Rosewater opined that 2/2 has never made great sense for a Bear. However, the tokens created by Dancing from Dark to Dawn still adhere to the old statistics.
paragraphs.section: Cards

paragraphs.text: Large Bear is a hybrid colorshifted version of Quaketusk Boar , from red into black-green.
